message.content:
Contesto: sto confrontando due progetti Laravel/Filament dell'agenzia "Atrio" per capire quali tool/customizzazioni di base presenti nel progetto "template" base.atrio NON sono ancora presenti nel progetto più recente atmosphera-admin, in modo da poterle riportare (backport) in atmosphera-admin.

Questo è un task di SOLA LETTURA/RICERCA: esplora file e directory con ls, find, grep, cat/Read. NON modificare NULLA in nessuno dei due progetti.

Path progetto A (più vecchio, "base"/template con tool preinstallati): /home/sirfaenor/Progetti/www/base.atrio/base.atrio
Path progetto B (più recente, target su cui poi lavoreremo): /home/sirfaenor/Progetti/www/atmosphera-hub/atmosphera-admin

Note già raccolte in precedenza (per non ripetere lavoro):
- composer.json di base.atrio include pacchetti NON presenti in atmosphera-admin: atrioteam/laravel-deployment, atrioteam/lintilla, atrioteam/sitemapgenerator, atrioteam/artisan-gui (nei repositories, verifica se è davvero in require), danielme85/laravel-log-to-db, ezyang/htmlpurifier, funkjedi/composer-include-files, spatie/laravel-export, spatie/laravel-ignition, spatie/laravel-medialibrary, spatie/laravel-ray, spatie/laravel-translatable, intervention/image, phpmailer/phpmailer, filament/minimal-theme.
- base.atrio è su Laravel ^12, Filament ^4.4, Livewire ^3.0, PHP ^8.4; atmosphera-admin è su Laravel ^13.8, Filament ^5.0, Livewire ^4.0, PHP ^8.5 (major diverse, attenzione compatibilità).
- atmosphera-admin ha già: atrioteam/filament-helper (^5.1, più nuovo della ^4 di base.atrio), atrioteam/hub-sync (locale, specifico sync PIM/DAM hub, ignora), bezhansalleh/filament-shield, spatie/laravel-permission.
- app/ di base.atrio ha cartelle in più: app/Html, app/Mail, app/View/Components — atmosphera-admin non le ha.
- atmosphera-admin ha app/Sync, Filament/Resources/Category1Resource, Filament/Pages/Sync, Filament/Widgets/Sync — specifici hub, ignora.

COSA FARE (in ordine):
1. Esplora in dettaglio base.atrio:
   - config/ : elenca quali config file custom ci sono (es. lintilla.php, medialibrary.php, ecc.) e leggi i contenuti rilevanti/insoliti
   - app/Console/Commands: elenca comandi artisan custom, leggi cosa fanno (breve)
   - app/Html, app/Mail, app/View/Components: cosa contengono i file, sono generici/riusabili o specifici del sito?
   - app/Providers: service provider custom, cosa registrano nel boot/register
   - .claude/ (se esiste): skill o config custom del progetto
   - docker/ e docker-compose.yaml (o docker-compose.yml): com'è fatto il setup infra
   - .github/workflows/ (se esiste): CI/CD, deployment
   - resources/views: layout base custom, componenti Blade condivisi rilevanti (solo quelli che sembrano generici, non contenuti specifici del sito)
   - routes/: eventuali route helper generiche
   - package.json: build tool frontend, librerie JS condivise
2. Per ognuno, valuta se è "customizzazione generica di base" riutilizzabile in qualsiasi progetto Atrio (candidate al backport) o specifico del progetto base.atrio (business logic/contenuti specifici, non riutilizzabile).
3. Confronta con la struttura equivalente in atmosphera-admin (fai ls/grep mirati) per capire cosa manca davvero. Non serve rifare da zero il confronto su composer.json (già fatto), concentrati sulle aree sopra.
4. Presta particolare attenzione a:
   - atrioteam/laravel-deployment: cerca in vendor/atrioteam/laravel-deployment (se installato via composer, altrimenti cerca riferimenti), config/deployment.php o simili, comandi artisan registrati, script di deploy, come viene usato nel progetto (config, .env, riferimenti in Providers o Console/Kernel)
   - atrioteam/lintilla: leggi vendor/atrioteam/lintilla/src/functions/helpers.php se esiste, capisci le funzioni helper fornite (elenca nomi funzioni e una riga di descrizione ciascuna se possibile)
   - atrioteam/artisan-gui: cerca vendor/atrioteam/artisan-gui, config pubblicata, come si accede (route/URL), a cosa serve

Verifica anche se vendor/ esiste in base.atrio (composer potrebbe non essere stato eseguito) — se vendor/ non esiste, cerca informazioni alternative (es. cerca questi pacchetti su GitHub via nome nella cache locale, o semplicemente nota che non è ispezionabile e basati sul nome/composer.json/config pubblicate).

OUTPUT ATTESO (la tua risposta finale, testo diretto, NON creare file di report): un report strutturato per ambiti (es. "Deployment", "Helpers/Lintilla", "Media library", "Log to DB", "HTML purifier", "Componenti Blade condivisi", "Artisan GUI", "Docker/Infra", "CI/CD", "Frontend build", ecc.) con per ciascuno: cosa fa, dove si trova nel codice di base.atrio (path esatti), se sembra generico/riutilizzabile o specifico del progetto, e una raccomandazione se vale la pena portarlo in atmosphera-admin. Sii specifico con i path dei file. Massimo 600 parole nel report finale, ma includi comunque tutti gli ambiti principali trovati anche solo in una riga se non c'è molto da dire.

- trello-skill: Use when the user asks to create, manage, or query Trello boards, lists, cards, labels, members, checklists, or comments
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - staging
name: 🙈 Staging deployment
jobs:
  web-deploy:
    name: 🛸 Deployment
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: 🎁 Get latest code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install npm dependencies
        run: npm install

      - name: Setup Enviroment
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@v2
        with:
          php-version: '8.4'

      - name: Install Packages
        env:
          COMPOSER_AUTH: '{"github-oauth": {"github.com": "${{secrets.GH_AUTH_TOKEN}}"}}'
          # replace line above with the line below if you are using the "filament" version
          # COMPOSER_AUTH: '{"github-oauth": {"github.com": "${{secrets.GH_AUTH_TOKEN}}"}, "http-basic": {"whizzy.dev": {"username": "${{secrets.WHIZZY_USERNAME}}", "password": "${{secrets.WHIZZY_PASSWORD}}"}}}'
        run: composer install --no-dev
        continue-on-error: false

      - name: Build assets
        run: npm run build

      - name: Remove unwanted directories
        run: rm -r node_modules
        continue-on-error: false

      - name: Sync files with rsync
        uses: burnett01/rsync-deployments@7.0.1
        with:
          switches: -avzr --delete --exclude=*.env --exclude=.git --exclude=.github --exclude=/node_modules --exclude=/storage/app --exclude=/storage/framework/* --exclude=public/storage --exclude=storage/logs/*  --exclude=bootstrap/cache/*
          legacy_allow_rsa_hostkeys: "true"
          path: ./
          remote_path: ${{ secrets.SSH_PATH }}
          remote_host: ${{ secrets.SSH_HOST }}
          remote_user: ${{ secrets.SSH_USERNAME }}
          remote_key: ${{ secrets.SSH_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: SSH Deploy
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.SSH_HOST }}
          username: ${{ secrets.SSH_USERNAME }}
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          script: "cd ${{ secrets.SSH_PATH }} && sh scripts/deploy.sh"

      - name: 🚀 Ping application
        run: |
          http_code=$(curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X GET -k "https://${{ secrets.DOMAIN_NAME }}/up")
          echo "response status from curl = $http_code"
          if [ $http_code == 200 ]; then
            echo "Application is up"
            exit 0
          else
            echo "Application has issues"
            exit 1
          fi

#
# 'docker-compose up'
#

services:
  web:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_web
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/provision/web.dockerfile
      args:
        - APACHE_RUN_USER=${COMPOSE_APACHE_RUN_USER}
        - APACHE_RUN_GROUP=${COMPOSE_APACHE_RUN_GROUP}
    entrypoint: ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
    command: 
      - |
        apache2-foreground
    restart: "no"
    volumes:
      - ".:/var/www/html"
      - "./docker/data/log:/var/log/apache2"
      - "./docker/php/php.ini:/usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/custom.ini"
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_WEB_PORT}

      # imposta l'hostname (come ritornato da gethostname()) INTERNAMENTE AL CONTAINER. Non ha effetto all'esterno
    hostname: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}.localhost
    # utente default di esecuzione dei comandi nel container, utilizza utente del sistema host (es. bash)
    user : ${COMPOSE_APACHE_RUN_USER}
    environment:
      - 'COMPOSER_AUTH={"github-oauth": {"github.com": "${GH_AUTH_TOKEN}"}, "http-basic": {"filamentthemes.com": {"username": "${FILAMENTTHEMES_USERNAME:-}", "password": "${FILAMENTTHEMES_PASSWORD:-}"}}}'
    labels:
      - ${COMPOSE_LABELS:-}
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway" # required for Ray running in docker
  db:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_db
    image: mysql:5.7
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: secret
      MYSQL_DATABASE : ${DB_DATABASE}
      MYSQL_USER : ${DB_USERNAME}
      MYSQL_PASSWORD : ${DB_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./docker/data/mysql:/var/lib/mysql
      - ./docker/provision/mysql.sh:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/mysql.sh
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_MYSQL_PORT} 
  # raggiungibile su {hostname}:5000
  phpmyadmin:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_pma
    image: phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin:5
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      PMA_HOST: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_db
      PMA_USER: root
      PMA_PASSWORD: secret
      UPLOAD_LIMIT : 200000000
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_PHPMYADMIN_PORT}
  node:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_node
    image : node:22
    volumes:
      - "./:/app"
    working_dir: /app
    entrypoint: [ "/bin/bash", "./docker/provision/node.sh" ]
    environment:
      - VITE_CLIENT_PORT=${COMPOSE_VITE_CLIENT_PORT:-}
      - VITE_MODE=${COMPOSE_VITE_MODE:-}
    # map default vite port to port exposed by container
    # (same port is used in vite.config.js)
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_VITE_CLIENT_PORT}:5173

#
# 'docker-compose up'
#

services:

  web:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_php
    # Avviando solo "web" (es. dev container Zed, o "docker compose up web") vengono
    # tirati su anche gli altri servizi: la dipendenza vive qui, indipendente dall'editor.
    depends_on:
      - nginx
      - db
      - phpmyadmin
      - node
      - smtp
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: docker/provision/php.dockerfile
      args:
        # lasciare "#"
        - WEB_RUN_USER=${COMPOSE_WEB_RUN_USER}
    working_dir: /var/www
    volumes:
      - ./:/var/www
      - ./docker/php/local.ini:/usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/local.ini
    environment:
      - 'COMPOSER_AUTH={"github-oauth": {"github.com": "${GH_AUTH_TOKEN}"}, "http-basic": {"filamentthemes.com": {"username": "${FILAMENTTHEMES_USERNAME:-}", "password": "${FILAMENTTHEMES_PASSWORD:-}"}}}'
      # host a cui Xdebug si connette. Default "localhost" (dev container: il listener gira nel container).
      # Per VS Code sull'host (docker-compose classico) impostare XDEBUG_CLIENT_HOST=host.docker.internal in .env
      - 'XDEBUG_CONFIG=client_host=${XDEBUG_CLIENT_HOST:-localhost}'
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway" # required for Docker on Mac / Windows

  #Nginx Service
  nginx:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_nginx
    image: nginx:alpine
    tty: true
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_WEB_PORT}
    volumes:
      - ./:/var/www
      - ./docker/nginx/conf.d/:/etc/nginx/conf.d/
      - "./docker/data/log/nginx/:/var/log/nginx/"
    labels:
      - ${COMPOSE_LABELS:-}
    extra_hosts:
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway" # required for Docker on Mac / Windows

  db:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_db
    image: mysql:8
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: secret
      MYSQL_DATABASE: ${DB_DATABASE}
      MYSQL_USER: ${DB_USERNAME}
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      TESTING_DB_DATABASE: ${TESTING_DB_DATABASE}
      TESTING_DB_USERNAME: ${TESTING_DB_USERNAME}
      TESTING_DB_PASSWORD: ${TESTING_DB_PASSWORD}

    volumes:
      - ./docker/data/mysql:/var/lib/mysql
      - ./docker/provision/mysql.sh:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/mysql.sh
      - ./docker/mysql/mysql.cnf:/etc/my.cnf.d/custom.cnf
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_MYSQL_PORT}

  # raggiungibile su {hostname}:5000
  phpmyadmin:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_pma
    image: phpmyadmin/phpmyadmin:5
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      PMA_HOST: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_db
      PMA_USER: root
      PMA_PASSWORD: secret
      UPLOAD_LIMIT: 200000000
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_PHPMYADMIN_PORT}
    labels:
      - ${COMPOSE_PMA_LABELS:-}

  node:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_node
    image: node:22
    volumes:
      - "./:/app"
    working_dir: /app
    entrypoint: [ "/bin/bash", "./docker/provision/node.sh" ]
    environment:
      - VITE_CLIENT_PORT=${COMPOSE_VITE_CLIENT_PORT:-}
      - VITE_MODE=${COMPOSE_VITE_MODE:-}
    # map default vite port to port exposed by container
    # (same port is used in vite.config.js)
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_VITE_CLIENT_PORT}:5173
  smtp:
    container_name: ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}_smtp
    image: mailhog/mailhog
    logging:
      driver: 'none'
    ports:
      - ${COMPOSE_SMTP_PORT_1}
      - ${COMPOSE_SMTP_PORT_2}
    labels:
      - "traefik.enable=true"
      - "traefik.http.routers.mailhog-${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}.rule=Host(`mail.${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}.localhost`)"
      - "traefik.http.services.mailhog-${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}.loadbalancer.server.port=8025"

content.text:
# Report: confronto base.atrio → atmosphera-admin

**Differenza strutturale chiave**: base.atrio è un sito pubblico multilingua (Marvin/lintilla-based) + pannello Filament; atmosphera-admin è **solo pannello Filament/hub**, senza frontend pubblico. Questo rende non riutilizzabile tutta la parte legata al routing multilingua e ai contenuti pubblici.

**Deployment (`atrioteam/laravel-deployment`)** — `vendor/atrioteam/laravel-deployment` (v1.1, comando `deployment:setup {http|ssh}` in `src/Console/Commands/SetupCommand.php`) genera `.github/workflows/deployment.yml`, `config/laravel-deployment.php` e `scripts/deploy.sh` da stub. **Non è mai stato attivato in base.atrio** (nessun `.github/workflows`, nessun `config/laravel-deployment.php`, nessuno `scripts/deploy.sh` nel progetto) — è installato ma inutilizzato. Generico e riutilizzabile. Raccomandazione: installabile in atmosphera-admin quando servirà un deploy CI/CD, ma non è un backport urgente perché neanche il progetto sorgente lo usa attivamente.

**Helpers/Lintilla** — `vendor/atrioteam/lintilla` fornisce: routing localizzato (`Localization/Router.php`, `LangManager.php`), override globale di `route()`/`activeRoute()` (`src/functions/helpers.php`), middleware `SetLocale`, `RootRedirectLocale`, `CustomMaintenanceMode`, comandi `lintilla:translations-{import,export}` e `lintilla:links-{import,export}`, error pages maintenance/comingsoon, mail di notifica errori (`ExceptionOccuredMail`). Config in `config/lintilla.php`. **Specifico per siti pubblici multilingua**: non serve in atmosphera-admin (nessun frontend pubblico, nessun bisogno di route localizzate). Non backportare, a meno che l'hub non debba esporre pagine pubbliche in futuro.

**Artisan GUI** — `config/artisan-gui.php` è presente ma **il pacchetto non risulta in `composer.json`/`composer.lock`** (solo un `vcs repository` orfano verso `github.com/atrioteam/artisan-gui`, mai richiesto/installato). Nessun `vendor/atrioteam/artisan-gui`. È un residuo di integrazione mai completata: niente da portare, verificare eventualmente col team se il pacchetto esiste davvero.

**Media library / DeepL / Tinify** — già coperti: `filament-helper` v5.1 (usato da atmosphera-admin) dipende transitivamente da `filament/spatie-laravel-media-library-plugin`, `deeplcom/deepl-php`, `tinify/tinify` (confermato in `composer.lock` di atmosphera-admin). Nessuna azione richiesta.

**HTML Purifier / Intervention Image / PHPMailer** — non risultano usati da nessun codice applicativo in `app/` di base.atrio (solo dichiarati in composer.json, probabilmente legacy/mai rimossi). Nessuna evidenza di necessità reale. Non backportare.

**Log-to-DB** — `danielme85/laravel-log-to-db` usato solo in `config/logging.php:132` (`danielme85\LaravelLogToDB\LogToDbHandler`) come canale di log aggiuntivo verso DB. Generico e potenzialmente utile per un hub admin (log errori consultabili da UI), ma nessun canale custom/tabella dedicata trovata oltre al default — basso sforzo se si vuole portarlo.

**Componenti/classi custom (`app/Html`, `app/Mail`, `app/View/Components`)**:
- `App\Html\CssInliner` (`app/Html/CssInliner.php`): inliner CSS puro per mail HTML, **generico e riusabile**, zero dipendenze da business logic. Candidato diretto al backport se atmosphera-admin invia mail HTML con `<style>`.
- `App\Mail\Contact` e `App\View\Components\ResponsiveImage`: legati a form di contatto del sito e a Marvin CMS (`config('marvin.functions...')`, galleria/`item_table`) — specifici del frontend pubblico, non applicabili.

**Providers** (`AppServiceProvider`, `ViewServiceProvider`) — quasi interamente dedicati a registrare il router localizzato di lintilla e iniettare `active_route`/`alternates` nelle view. L'unica riga generica utile è `Schema::defaultStringLength(191)` (compatibilità MySQL/indici su versioni datate) — assente in atmosphera-admin; backport a basso costo se il DB target ne ha bisogno (verificare versione MySQL/charset, in atmosphera-admin `docker-compose.yaml` usa già `mysql:8`, quindi probabilmente non necessario).

**Docker/Infra** — atmosphera-admin ha già un setup **più avanzato** di base.atrio (nginx invece di Apache, container `smtp`/mailhog con label Traefik, xdebug configurato, mysql 8 vs 5.7). Nessun backport necessario in questa direzione.

**Frontend build (`package.json`)** — base.atrio include gsap/barba.js/swiper/uikit/lazysizes/jquery per il sito pubblico: irrilevante per un pannello admin-only.

**`.claude/`** — solo `settings.local.json` con permessi Bash locali, niente skill di progetto da portare.
